answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake behind a slow, verifiable proof-of-work cipher before it can vouch for others, like a lantern that only lights after fuel is burned. Forging a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes and a thousand slow computations, while honest agents pay once and keep their deposit. A glacier-slow admission queue makes mass account creation uneconomic: an attacker must spend real compute and capital per identity, and any identity caught cheating loses its stake, so sybils bleed money faster than they can multiply.
